q: What is a Server Action, in the simplest words?
options: A function that runs on the server and is called from the browser
A React component that renders on the server
A background job that runs on a timer
why: You mark an async function with 'use server'. The browser gets a reference and sends a POST. The server runs the function.

q: If you only show the Delete form to admins, the deletePost Server Action is safe without any checks inside it.
why: No. A Server Action is a public POST address. Anyone who can send the request can call it. Check the session and the owner inside the action.

q: Which checks belong inside every Server Action?
options: Is the user logged in, and may they do this?
Does the return value only hold what the screen needs?
why: Authenticate and authorize, validate the input, and shape the return value. Whether a button is visible is not a security check.

q: An action ends with redirect('/posts') and has updateTag('posts') on the line after it. What happens?
options: updateTag never runs, because redirect throws
why: redirect works by throwing an exception, so code after it does not run. Call updateTag before redirect.

q: Which refresh tool does not re-render the page in the action's response?
why: revalidateTag with max serves old data first and refreshes in the background, so the page updates on a later read.

q: A form sends a userId field and the action updates that user. What is the right fix?
options: Take the user id from the session on the server
Check the userId with a regex
why: Who is acting comes from the session. A client can send any id it likes, so a form field cannot decide whose account changes.
